about.title: What is Satlas?
about.intro: Curious what satellites are passing over your country right now? This site answers that at a glance.

why.title: Why I built it
why.body: Most satellite trackers focus on what you can see from your own location. Few show what's flying over an entire country, so I built one.

how.title: How it works
how.body: Each satellite's current position is computed from public orbital data (TLEs) using a standard propagation formula (SGP4). We then check which country that coordinate falls over.
how.refresh: We automatically pull fresh catalog and orbit data twice a day and restart calculations from those measurements. Satellites drift slightly over time due to atmospheric drag and small gravitational variations, so the longer the same computation runs forward, the more its result diverges from reality. Thanks to this refresh cycle, the residual position error stays very small within this site's 24-hour window.

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: Satellite categories follow our data source (CelesTrak) as-is. Classified satellites — for example reconnaissance — whose orbits are not public are not included. Country borders come from a public map dataset (Natural Earth) at a coarse resolution, so very small islands may be missing.

source.title: Sources
source.intro: Code and data are all open.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: We use Vercel Analytics for visitor statistics: cookieless, aggregate page views only. No personally identifiable information is collected.
